doc.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024

title: Playing along with Chet Baker, Miles and Maynard Ferguson
summary: As a young trumpeter he played along with records; Chet Baker was playable, Dizzy and Maynard were out of reach.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I’m sorry, was Gerry Mulligan in your consciousness at that time?

Maybe through Chet Baker. Because when I really started to get interested in jazz I would have probably been eighth or ninth grade, and I was trying to find records of trumpet players even though I didn’t — maybe didn’t know who they were — to play along with, or to try to play with. And so I had come across Chet Baker. And Chet was actually one that I could actually somewhat play along with. Miles, you know, a little bit, but then Dizzy Gillespie, you know no. You know I found a Dizzy Gillespie record and you know, I couldn’t do that.
How about Maynard Ferguson, right? Oh there’s an easy one.

Yeah, and I’m of the age to where Maynard was like the big star in the ‘70s you know and I mean so all the, you know everybody, all the trumpet players especially idolized Maynard Ferguson. And I, you know I loved it too but I knew that I couldn’t do that and I didn’t know if that was something that I would ever be able to do, but I recognized the fact that I could only go so far with the Maynard things before I’d have to go down an octave or two.
